reasons: Cascade behaviour is not visible in this code.

terms.meaning: a short code that lets someone join a crew
automatic deletion of records linked to a record that is deleted

sections.name: File setup, memberSelect
sections.title: Shared member fields
sections.what: Brings in the database client and the public user shape, and defines which member fields are returned.
sections.why: Likely reason: the same member details are used by several crew queries.

sections.name: findCrewWithMembers
sections.title: Crew with its members
sections.what: Loads one crew by ID with its name, invite code, owner and member list, oldest members first.
sections.why: Likely reason: the crew page needs everything in one read.
sections.watch_out: The invite code comes back with the crew, so anyone who can read the crew can read the code.

sections.name: findCrew
sections.title: Crew basics
sections.what: Loads one crew by ID with only its name and owner.
sections.why: Likely reason: a light lookup for checks that do not need members.

sections.name: findCrewByCode
sections.title: Crew by invite code
sections.what: Finds a crew from its invite code.
sections.why: Likely reason: used when someone joins through a code or link.

sections.name: findMembership
sections.title: Membership check
sections.what: Finds whether a user belongs to a crew.
sections.why: Likely reason: many crew rules depend on it.

sections.name: listCrewsForUser
sections.title: Crews for a user
sections.what: Lists every crew a user belongs to, with member counts, oldest first.
sections.why: Likely reason: supports the crew list page.

sections.name: listMemberIds
sections.title: Member IDs in a crew
sections.what: Returns the IDs of everyone in a crew.
sections.why: Likely reason: needed to group or check crew members.

sections.name: countMembers
sections.title: Member count
sections.what: Counts the members of a crew.
sections.why: Likely reason: used to decide whether an owner may leave.

sections.name: insertCrew
sections.title: Creating a crew
sections.what: Creates a crew and its first member, the owner, in one write.
sections.why: Likely reason: the owner is always a member from the start.

sections.name: insertMember
sections.title: Adding a member
sections.what: Adds one user to a crew.
sections.why: Likely reason: used when someone joins.
sections.watch_out: A duplicate join is stopped by a database rule, so the caller must handle that failure.

sections.name: deleteMember
sections.title: Removing a member
sections.what: Removes one user from a crew.
sections.why: Likely reason: used when someone leaves or is removed.

sections.name: deleteCrew
sections.title: Deleting a crew
sections.why: Likely reason: used when the last member leaves.
sections.watch_out: Whether memberships and other linked records are removed too depends on database settings not shown here.

sections.name: setInviteCode
sections.title: Changing the invite code
sections.what: Saves a new invite code for a crew and returns it.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the owner shut out old links.
sections.watch_out: The new code can clash with an existing one, so the caller must retry.

sections.name: setOwner
sections.title: Changing the owner
sections.what: Sets a different user as the crew's owner.
sections.why: Likely reason: used when ownership is handed over.
sections.watch_out: This does not check that the new owner is a member. The service layer does.

sections.name: isBlockedBy
sections.title: Block check
sections.what: Reports whether one user has blocked another.
sections.why: Likely reason: used to stop blocked people from joining.

sections.name: blockedIdsFor
sections.title: Blocked users list
sections.what: Lists the IDs of users a given user has blocked.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the crew page hide blocked people's names.

summary: Database access for crews, memberships, ownership, invite codes and blocks.
why: Likely reason: keeps database access out of the crew rules.
how: 1. Read crews and their members. 2. Create, add, remove or delete crews and members. 3. Change the invite code or the owner. 4. Check and list blocks.
inputs: Crew IDs, user IDs, names, and invite codes.
outputs: Crew records, member lists, counts, yes or no answers, or nothing.
risks: Invite codes come back with crew reads. Deleting a crew depends on database cascade rules that are not shown here.
debug: If a deleted crew leaves stray members, check the database cascade rules. If a join fails with a duplicate, check the membership uniqueness rule.
